rows.jp: 「いそげっ、いそげっ」
そして。
「ついたぁ」
「はー、はー、ぜー、ぜー」
霧がバテていた。
「おー、いいタイミング！」
美希は全然平気だった。
rows.en: Miki was not winded in the slightest.

rows.jp: 現金な娘だ。
「暗くなる前につけたのはいいけど、暗くなる前に帰らないとな」
rows.en: “It’s good we made it before dark, but we also have to get back before dark.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's good we got here before it got dark, but we can't get home before it's dark, so..."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that they must return before it gets dark. The English says that returning before dark is impossible, reversing obligation into inability.
ghs.remedy: we need to get home before it gets dark

highlights.text: we can't get home before it's dark

rows.jp: 一応、この太一袋には懐中電灯も入っているが。
rows.en: I did have a flashlight in the Taichi Bag, just in case.

ghs.en: Just in case, however, I got a big flashlight in my Taichi Bag as well.

rows.jp: 「夕日が見たかったのでちょうどいいです」
rows.en: “I wanted to see the sunset, so this is perfect.”

ghs.en: Miki: "I wanted to see the sunset, so this is just right."

rows.jp: 「よいしょっとー！」
そして美希は、両手の花（片方俺）を引き寄せた。
rows.en: Miki drew in the flowers on either side of her—one of whom was me.

ghs.en: And then, Miki drew towards herself the flowers she had in both hands (one of them me).

rows.jp: 「おっと」
「きゃん」
「一番きれいなのは沈む直前かなー」
rows.en: “It’s prettiest just before it disappears, I think.”

ghs.en: Miki: "It's the prettiest just before it totally sinks I thiiink!"

rows.jp: もう三十分くらいだろうか。

ghs.en: Seems there'll be no more than thirty minutes to go.

rows.jp: 「……はぁ、お腹すいたなぁ」
「なんか食べ物はないんですか、先輩？」
「あるよ」
カンパンの残りを出した。
rows.en: I brought out the remaining hardtack.

ghs.en: I took out the leftover Kanpan.

rows.jp: 「そのうらぶれたボクサーが使ってるみたいな袋、なんでも入ってますか？」
rows.en: “Does that bag for washed-up boxers contain everything?”

ghs.en: Miki: "That bag that looks like it's used by a boxer that's gone to the dogs, does it have everything in it or something?"

rows.jp: 「太一袋だから」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yes, because it's the Taichi Bag."

rows.jp: 「のどかわいたです」

ghs.en: Miki: "My throat is a bit parched."

rows.jp: 「はいよ」
水筒。
「……す、すごい」
欲しそうだった。

ghs.en: She seemed to really want it.

rows.jp: 「ビスケット食べる？」
曜子ちゃんが作ったやつだ。
「もらいます！　はい、霧っち」
二人は旺盛に食べた。
「このビスケット……おいしいですねぇ」

ghs.en: Miki: "These biscuits are... really delicious, aren't they!"

rows.jp: 「本当……柔らかくて、甘くて……」
「曜子ちゃんのビスケットだから」
「愛されてますねー」
「偏愛されてるんだよ」
ありがたい度より迷惑度は高い。
rows.en: Honestly, I was more annoyed than grateful.

ghs.en: The level of annoyance is higher than the level of thankfulness.

rows.jp: 「でも監視カメラはやめてほしいよなぁ」
rows.en: “I do wish she would stop with the surveillance cameras.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But I wish she stopped with the surveillance cameras at least."

rows.jp: 俺の部屋。
もう電源が断たれているので使用はされてないだろうけど。
rows.en: The power was out now, so they could not still be in use.

ghs.en: As the electricity has been cut I don't think she'll be able to employ them anymore, at least.

rows.jp: 「……で、美希はなにを待ってるの？」
rows.en: “...So what are you waiting for, Miki?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...so, what are you waiting for, Miki?"

rows.jp: 「夕日だよ？」

ghs.assessment: The Japanese reply identifies the sunset and means 'what else?' The English substitutes twilight and contains the grammatical error 'was else.'

rows.jp: 「これって夕日でしょ？」

ghs.assessment: The Japanese asks whether the visible phenomenon is the setting sun. The English calls it twilight, obscuring the following distinction between sunset and afterglow.

rows.jp: 「美希っちが待ってるのは、余光だよ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "What Miki's waiting for is the afterglow."

rows.jp: 「よこう？」
「日が没したあとさ、空がものすごいオレンジ色になるだろ？　残照とも言うけど」
rows.en: “After the sun goes down, the sky turns this incredible orange. It’s also called the evening glow.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "After the sun sinks, you know, when the sky turns that amazing shade of orange? It's the crepuscular light, in other words."

rows.jp: 「それを三人で見る。いい感じじゃないですか」
rows.en: “And the three of us are going to watch it together. Doesn’t that sound nice?”

ghs.en: Miki: "We'll be looking at it, all three of us. Doesn't that feel so great?"

rows.jp: デートというか、多感なオトモダチ同士って感じだな。
rows.en: Less a date than three impressionable friends spending time together.

ghs.en: More than a date, this feels more like bonding between emotionally sensitive friends.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says this feels less like a date and more like an outing among sensitive friends. 'More than a date' reverses the comparison by suggesting something beyond or more significant than a date.

rows.jp: 「にゃんにきにゃかにゃか♪　にゃんにきにゃかにゃか♪」
「ぉっぱいさわんないでよ」
ま、楽しそうだからいいか。
rows.en: Well, she seemed to be enjoying herself.

ghs.en: Well, we're having fun so it's good.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese observes that the girl appears to be enjoying herself. The English changes this external observation into a claim that the whole group is having fun.
ghs.remedy: she looks like she's having fun

rows.jp: 「……なあ、性欲をもてあます霧ちん」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...say, Kiri-chin with the sexual desire out of control."

rows.jp: 「水を吹くな」
「話したの！？　見せたの！？」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Did she talk about it?! Did she show them to you?!"

rows.jp: 「見せてないよ。平気平気」

ghs.en: Miki: "I showed nothing. It's alright, it's alright!"

rows.jp: だいたい何があったのか想像ついてきた。
rows.en: I was beginning to imagine what had happened.

ghs.en: I could imagine the general outline of what happened.

rows.jp: 「二人がはじめて部活に参加した日、覚えてる？」
rows.en: “Remember the first day the two of you joined the club?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Remember that day, when you two first participated to club?"

rows.jp: 「……ええ、一応」
「あんなの、忘れようとしても無理です」
rows.en: “I couldn’t forget that if I tried.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Even if I wanted to forget that stuff it is impossible to."

rows.jp: 「なかなか入れてくれなかったもんね」
rows.en: “You wouldn’t let us in for ages.”

ghs.en: Miki: "We weren't able to get in that readily, no."

rows.jp: 「……んー、試験が終わるまではね。適性があるので」
rows.en: “...Only until the examinations were over. Aptitude matters.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...hmmm, not until the end of the exams, right. Because of aptitude."

rows.jp: 自由に部活に入れるわけでもないのだった。
rows.en: Students could not simply join any club they pleased.

ghs.en: Joining up clubs wasn't left to volition.

rows.jp: 希望は通るが。
rows.en: Their preferences were honored, at least.

ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that students' preferences or requests are honored. The English only says that wishes are communicated, changing whether they are acted upon.
ghs.remedy: They do honor our preferences, though.

rows.jp: 群青はその都合上、大学をのぞくエレベーター式になっている。
rows.en: For practical reasons, Gunjo was organized as one continuous school through every level except university.

ghs.en: For convenience of management, Gunjou was made into an elevator school with all but post-secondary education.

rows.jp: 霧が来たのは去年の夏。
rows.en: Kiri had arrived the previous summer.

ghs.en: Kiri had come on Summer of last year,

rows.jp: 美希はそのもう少し後だった。
二人とも一個下の三年生として編入された。
rows.en: Both transferred into the third year, one grade below us.

ghs.en: The two of them were admitted as third years one school level below.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the two entered as third-years one year below the narrator. 'One school level below' suggests a different division of schooling rather than the adjacent year or grade.

rows.jp: 校舎自体は同じで、その頃にも多少は顔を合わせていた。
rows.en: We shared the same school building, so I had seen them around before then.

ghs.en: The school building itself is the same, so even in those times there was some face-to-face.

rows.jp: 「あれは面白かった。忘れないです」
rows.en: “That was fun. I’ll never forget it.”

rows.jp: 「……面白かったかなあ」
「二人に素敵なニックネームもつけてやったな。俺が」
rows.en: “I even gave you two marvelous nicknames.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And you two even got a splendid nickname. From me!"

rows.jp: 「えーと、島先輩がインモラルで、たいち先輩は愛貴族でしたっけ？」
rows.en: “Let me think. Shima was Immoral, and you were the Love Noble, right?”

ghs.en: Miki: "Uhmmm, so Shima-senpai was Immoral, Taichi-senpai was the Aristocrat of Love, right?"

rows.jp: よく記憶している。
「……愛貴族って、先輩のトークに頻繁に出てくる単語ですよね」
rows.en: “...‘Love Noble’ is one of those phrases you use all the time, isn’t it?”

ghs.en: Miki: "...'Aristocrat of Love' is the kind of thing that comes up frequently in your speech, Senpai."

rows.jp: 「愛奴隷とか愛人形とか……最低」

ghs.en: Kiri: "And love slave, and love doll... disgusting!"

rows.jp: 「いっそ最低奴隷にしたらどうですか？」
rows.en: “Why not just call yourself the Lowest Slave?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "How about Disgusting Slave, should it not be that instead?"

rows.jp: 「ううむ……奴隷のさらに最低って、俺すごい底辺具合なんだな」
rows.en: “Hmm... Lower than a slave. I really am the lowest of the low.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Huuum... slave and furthermore disgusting, that's an awesomely low reputation I have, yes."

rows.jp: 「霧ちん毒ー」
「あとさ、桜庭の柿の種の説法とか覚えてる？」
rows.en: “And do you remember Sakuraba’s sermon on peanut-mix rice crackers?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And then, do you remember that sermon Sakuraba did on seeds of persimmon?"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese names Kaki no Tane, the established rice-cracker snack, in recalling Sakuraba's lecture. The English parses the compound literally as actual persimmon seeds and changes the object being discussed.

rows.jp: 霧が吹いた。
記憶していたらしい。

ghs.en: Seems like she has the memories.

rows.jp: 「そういえば、一つ質問があります」
rows.en: “Actually, there is something I’ve been meaning to ask.”

ghs.en: Miki: "On that topic, I have a question."

rows.jp: 「桜庭先輩の耳って悪いんですか？」
「ああ、鼓膜が痛んでるから」
「……知りませんでした」
「俺がやった」

ghs.en: Taichi: "I was the one who did that."

rows.jp: 霧が眉をひそめた。
「シャレになりません」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Do not make this a joke."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese evaluates the situation as too serious to be a joke. The English turns that reaction into an instruction not to make a joke, changing the utterance's function.

highlights.text: Do not make this a joke.

rows.jp: 「まあ聞け。原因はヤツにある」
rows.en: “Hear me out. It was his own fault.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, listen up. The blame lies with that guy."

rows.jp: 「……俺が下のガッコ時代の……んー、二年生くらいだったかな。学院祭があったのだ」
rows.en: “...Back when I was in the lower school... Hmm, I think I was a second-year. We held a school festival.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...when I was in the middle school... hmmm, second year or thereabouts, there was a school festival."

rows.jp: 「今はないですよね？」
rows.en: “We don’t have those anymore, do we?”

rows.jp: 「いろいろ問題起こったからね」

ghs.en: Taichi: "We had all sorts of problems, that's why."

rows.jp: 「当時もそりゃこぢんまりしていたものだった。やっぱ有識者数が少ないからね」%N※有識(うしき)＝喜怒哀楽、情緒を有すること
rows.en: “Even then, it was a modest little affair. There weren’t many sentients around, after all.”%N*Here, ‘sentient’ means possessing joy, anger, sorrow, pleasure, and emotion.

ghs.en:
Taichi: "Back then things were quiiite a bit snug. The number of 'Experts' was really low, that's why."
* 'Expert' = person in which the basic emotions (happiness, fear, sorrow, pleasure) are present.

rows.jp: 「で、やっぱり基本的には、周辺住民の賛同は欲しいわけだよ。こんな学校でも」
rows.en: “Still, even a school like ours wanted the goodwill of the surrounding community.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "So it's as you'd think, basically they wanted some approval from the residents around them. Even when the school is like this."

rows.jp: 「学院祭とはいっても、知らない人がどやどや来ると不安定になったりするヤツも多いんで、有志による劇みたいなことをやったんだ」
rows.en: “Calling it a school festival was generous. Letting crowds of strangers in made too many students unstable, so a group of volunteers put on a play instead.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "A school festival, well, because there's lots of guys who get unstable just at the bustle of footsteps of too many strangers, it was more like a play performed by volunteers."

rows.jp: 「あの年は……シェイクスピアだった。演目は―――」
rows.en: “That year... it was Shakespeare. The play was—”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That year... it was Shakespeare. The play was---"

rows.jp: 「ロミオとジュリエット」
そう。
「ベタですねー」
「うむ。もはやベティだった」

ghs.assessment: The Japanese extends the preceding beta or hackneyed joke by personifying it as the name Betty. 'Neya' has no support in the source and breaks both the wordplay and the explanation that follows.
ghs.remedy: It was practically Betty by then.

rows.jp: 「ベタってのを擬人化して……」
rows.en: “He took ‘corny’ and turned it into a woman’s name...”

rows.jp: 「……ああ、そういう意味……」
「フフフ。美希、ナイスフォロー」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hoh hoh hoh! Excellent follow-up Miki!"

rows.jp: 「いえ」
「決めてンだ。自分のギャグを自分で解説するときは、死ぬ時だけだってな」
rows.en: “I made a vow long ago: the day I explain one of my own jokes is the day I die.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I made up my mind. The only time I'll explain my own jokes by myself will be the time of my death."

rows.jp: 「……どっかの映画のセリフみたい」
rows.en: “...That sounds like a line from some movie.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...that sounds like a line from some movie."

rows.jp: 「ま、とにかくシェイクスピアだ。日本名にしたら……フッ、振槍さんってとこか」
rows.en: “Anyway, Shakespeare. Put that into Japanese and you would get... heh. Mr. Spearshaker.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, anyway, Shakespeare. If I'd have to make the name in Japanese, let's see, kanji for shake read 'furu' and kanji for spear read 'yari', so..."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese completes the literalized name joke with 'Furuyari-san.' The English explains the component readings but omits the resulting name that the next reaction answers.
ghs.remedy: Well, anyway, Shakespeare. In Japanese that would make him... Mr. Furuyari, I suppose.

highlights.text: Well, anyway, Shakespeare. If I'd have to make the name in Japanese, let's see, kanji for shake read 'furu' and kanji for spear read 'yari', so...

rows.jp: 美希は身震いした。
「……ひねろうというこれっぽっちの意志さえ感じられないっっ！」
rows.en: “Not one speck of effort to twist it into something clever!”

ghs.en: Miki: "...I can't feel the even tiniest intent of wanting to twist thiiings!"

rows.jp: 俺の実直さの虜がまた一人。
rows.en: Another slave to my uncompromising honesty.

ghs.en: Yet one more victim of my honesty.

rows.jp: 「ノーツイスト主義」
俺はうらぶれたボクサーのように、茜色の空を見あげた。
rows.en: Like a washed-up boxer, I gazed up at the crimson sky.

ghs.en: Just like a boxer that's gone to the dogs, I look up at the sky of madder red.

rows.jp: 「スペル合ってるのかな？」

ghs.en: Kiri: "But would that have even been spelled correctly?"

rows.jp: 「さあ？」

ghs.assessment: The Japanese means 'Who knows?' and answers uncertainty about the spelling. 'Who cares?' instead dismisses the question as unimportant.

rows.jp: 「配役をあててごらん！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Let us now go guess the cast!"

rows.jp: 「……先輩がロミオ、かな？」
「他の人って……当時誰がいたかわからない……」
rows.en: “But who else was there? I don’t know who attended back then...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "As for the rest... I dunno who was even there at that time..."

rows.jp: 「曜子ちゃんが一個上だった」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Youko-chan was one year above me."

rows.jp: 「じゃ、支倉先輩がジュリエット」
「残念。その逆」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Better luck next time. It was the opposite."

ghs.assessment: The Japanese jokes that the casting is a reversal because the two expected roles were swapped. The English interprets the expression as plot twists and loses the gender-role reversal being discussed.

rows.jp: 「そう。まあ当時は体格面で同じくらいだったんで、どっちがやっても平気だった」
rows.en: “Exactly. We were about the same size then, so either role worked.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Indeed. Well, around then our builds were sort of the same, so however we did it it'd be OK."

rows.jp: 「あとねー、他に劇ができるほど安定してるのいなかったから、全役俺と曜子ちゃんでやった」
rows.en: “And no one else was stable enough to perform, so Youko and I played every role.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And theeen, because there were no other people stable enough to do a play, all roles were performed by me and Youko-chan."

rows.jp: 「それって……学院祭？」

ghs.en: Miki: "And that... was a school festival?"

rows.jp: 「まあ、体面上」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, that was for appearance's sake."

rows.jp: 「劇自体は大成功だった。特に迫真のキッスシーンを……あのアマ……人前で……」
rows.en: "The play itself was a huge success. Especially the realistic kiss scene… that bitch… in front of everyone…"

ghs.en: Taichi: "The play itself was a big success. Particularly the realistic kiss scene... that bitch... in front of people..."

rows.jp: 「こ、この人泣いてる……」
「どうしたんだろう？」
「ちくしょう！　当時の俺には、まだ露出のケはなかったのに！！」
rows.en: "Damn it! At the time, I didn't even have a taste for exposure!!"

ghs.en: Taichi: "Dammit all! At that time, I didn't even have my exhibitionist streak!!!"

rows.jp: 「今はあるのかよ……」
「とにかく、口づけをかわす二人の口の間からだらだらとヨダレが流れていようが」
rows.en: "Anyway, even if drool dripped from between their mouths as they kissed,"

ghs.en: Taichi: "Anyway, in our reciprocal kiss saliva was schlooping down in the gap between our two mouths."

rows.jp: 「ヒロイン役の俺が逃れようとじたばたしているのに主人公役の方がサブミッションを決めていようが」
rows.en: "even if the heroine—me—struggled to escape while the protagonist kept locking in submissions,"

ghs.en: Taichi: "Because I was in the role of the heroine, I was to try to escape kicking and fighting, but Miss Protagonist over there decided the scene should end in submission,"

rows.jp: 「スカートの下で執拗に局部タッチをされていようが、誰一人気がつかないのが演劇の魔力だ」
rows.en: "even if I was persistently touched under my skirt—no one noticed a thing. That's the magic of theater."

ghs.en: Taichi: "and she went for an insistent underskirt genital touch, but not one person noticed. That is the magic of theater."

rows.jp: 「劇は大成功だった。俺は下着を替えた」
rows.en: "The play was a huge success. I changed my underwear."

ghs.en: Taichi: "The play was a great success. I had to change my underwear."

rows.jp: 「そこに新キャラ、桜庭登場～！」
rows.en: “And then a new character entered: Sakuraba!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And there we meet that new character, Sakuraba～!"

rows.jp: 「出た」
「ヤツは本能に忠実な男。いや、あまりにも忠実すぎる男だった」
rows.en: “Sakuraba was a man ruled by instinct. A man far too faithful to it.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That idiot was a man loyal to his instincts. Well, he was a man extremely loyal to his instincts."

rows.jp: 「桜庭は観劇に来た。そして一目惚れをした」
rows.en: “He came to see the play. And he fell in love at first sight.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Sakuraba came to the play. And then he was immediately smitten."

rows.jp: 「支倉先輩に……」
「違う、俺に」
「えええええええええええええっ！！」
鼓膜破れかけた。
「えーえー、桜庭先輩が太一先輩にーっ！？」
「ねえねえ、じゃあ桜庭先輩が全然女の子に興味ないって噂って？」
rows.en: “Wait, then what about that rumor that Sakuraba has no interest in girls?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Hey, hey, you heard the rumor that Sakuraba-senpai has no interest in women whatsoever?"

rows.jp: 「ひゃーーー！　どーなんだろー！」
「わっ、わあぁー」
「きゃーきゃー！」
うるせぇ……。
「で、どうなったんですか？」
「そのハモりなんかムカつく」
rows.en: “You two talking in unison is really getting on my nerves.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Those harmonics kinda piss me off."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese refers to the two girls saying the same line in harmony or unison. 'Harmonics' denotes acoustic overtones and does not identify their synchronized speech.

rows.jp: 「……とにかくだ。桜庭はあれで強引グマイウェイ。舞台袖にすぐあらわれた。花壇に植えてあった校長の花を勝手に摘んでな」
rows.en: “...Anyway. Sakuraba marches to the beat of his own bulldozer. He showed up backstage right away with flowers he’d helped himself to from the principal’s flower bed.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...bah, anyway. Sakuraba, in that, is stupidly Go-My-Way. He immediately showed up in the stage wings. He had up and picked some flowers that the headmaster planted in the flowerbed."

rows.jp: 「俺は驚いた。出会ってから告白まで、三秒。はやい、はやすぎた」
rows.en: “I was stunned. Three seconds from meeting me to declaring his love. Fast. Far too fast.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I was shocked. From meeting to confession it was three seconds. Fast, and way too fast."

rows.jp: 二人が息を詰めている。
……なんか話したくなくなってきたぞ。
rows.en: ...Suddenly I wasn’t so sure I wanted to keep telling this story.

ghs.en: ...turns out I don't really want to talk about this.

rows.jp: 「不幸なことに、その場に曜子ちゃんはいなかった」
rows.en: “Unfortunately, Youko was not there at the time.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "What a misfortune it was that Youko-chan wasn't there."

rows.jp: 「だが俺は冷静だった。だって俺は男。桜庭の愛を肉体的に受け入れるホールにも事欠く有様だった（大人のジョーク）」
rows.en: "But I stayed calm. Because I'm a man. I was hardly lacking a hole to physically receive Sakuraba's love (adult joke)."

ghs.en: Taichi: "But I remained composed. I'm a man after all. I am found to be missing the physical hole to accept Sakuraba's love (adult joke)."

rows.jp: 「だから俺は自らのシンボルを露出することで、男だということを証明してやった。これをシンボリズムという」
rows.en: "So I proved I was a man by exposing my own symbol. Call it symbolism."

ghs.en: Taichi: "Therefore, I exposed my symbol, providing evidence that I am a man. That is what is called 'symbolism'."

rows.jp: 「……嘘だね」
「うん、嘘だね」
「ギャグつまらないね」
「うん、でも我慢しよう。話はおもしろいもの」
rows.en: “It is, but let’s endure it. The story is interesting.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Yes, but let's bear with it. This story is very interesting."

rows.jp: 「……泣いていいか」
「だが桜庭は止まらなかった」
『男でもいい』
rows.en: ‘I don’t care if you’re a boy.’

rows.jp: 「そしてヤツは襲いかかってきた。実は俺には、ヤツを受け入れかねないホールに、一つばかし心当たりがあったのだ（大人のジョーク）」
rows.en: "And then he attacked me. Actually, I did have one possible hole that might receive him (adult joke)."

ghs.en: Taichi: "And with that the guy swooped on me. Truth is, I did have an idea about what hole I could use to receive the guy (adult joke)."

rows.jp: 「うをーーーーーーーっ！」
「そ、それって……」
楽しそうだなオイ。
rows.en: They were having far too much fun with this.

ghs.en: Having so much fun aren't you, dammit.

rows.jp: 「で、我が貞操を守るため、俺は平手を繰り出した。それがヤツの耳に当たって……まあちょっと怪我をさせてしまったのだ」
rows.en: “To preserve my chastity, I slapped him. It caught his ear and... well, did a little damage.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Then, to protect Our Chastity, I lunged at him with the palm of the hand. And I struck right on the ears... leaving him, well, with a bit of an injury it seems."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that the narrator delivered an open-handed slap to protect his own chastity. The English changes 'my' to 'our' and describes a vague lunge with a palm instead of the slap whose impact injured the ear.
ghs.remedy: to protect my chastity, I slapped him.

highlights.text: to protect Our Chastity, I lunged at him with the palm of the hand.

rows.jp: 「ああ、それでちょっと耳が……」

ghs.en: Miki: "Ahhh, that's why his hearing got a bit..."

rows.jp: 「あとで父親と一緒に謝罪しにきた。なにしろレイプ未遂だからな。まあこっちの責任は問われなかったよ」
rows.en: “He came over with his dad to apologize afterward. It was attempted rape, after all. Nobody held me responsible.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Later he came with his father and apologized. It was attempted rape after all. Well, my part in it was not questioned at least."

rows.jp: 「もともと人の話を聞かないヤツだが、さらに磨きがかかったらしい」
rows.en: “He never listened to people in the first place. Apparently the injury only honed the talent.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "He'd been a guy who didn't listen to what people say from the start, and now he seems to have improved on that a bit."

rows.jp: 「で、桜庭が病院に運ばれて……その場はそれですんだんだけど」
rows.en: “Sakuraba was taken to the hospital... and that seemed to be the end of it.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Then, Sakuraba was carried to the hospital... and there, that was all this ended up as."

rows.jp: 「進学したら、クライメイトにヤツがいた……」
rows.en: “Then I started at my new school—and there he was, in my class...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "When I advanced to High School, there he was, all acclimated..."

rows.jp: 「追いかけてきた？」
「たぶん……」
「で、二人はその後？」
rows.en: “And what happened between you after that?”

ghs.en: Miki: "And, what happened to you two afterwards?"

rows.jp: 「何もない！　というか、ヤツも別に俺の全角アスタリスクをどうこうする気はないらしい」%N※全角アスタリスク＝『＊』←コレ
rows.en: “Nothing! He does not even seem interested in doing anything to my full-width asterisk.”%N*Full-width asterisk = ‘＊.’

ghs.en:
Taichi: "Nothing! That is to say, he didn't seem to be in the spirit to invade my full-width asterisk."
* Full-width asterisk = 『＊』 ← this

rows.jp: 「プラトニック・ラ……」
「言うな」
頭を抱える。

ghs.en: I grab my head, at wits' end.

rows.jp: 「正直、複雑以外のどんな感情もない」
rows.en: “Honestly, ‘complicated’ is the only feeling I have.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Honestly, I can't have any emotion for him except for mixed ones."

rows.jp: 「それでイジメてるわけですね」

ghs.en: Miki: "And that is the reason for all the bullying."

rows.jp: 「……他にどんな反応をしろと」
rows.en: “...How else am I supposed to react?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...what reaction should I have other than that."

rows.jp: 「しかもあいつ、ほっとくと俺に異常に親切なんだ」
rows.en: “And if I leave him alone, he is abnormally kind to me.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Especially when that guy's abnormally kind to me if left alone."

rows.jp: 鳥肌が立ってきた。
「そんなのは一人でたくさん……というか、俺が求めてるのは普通の人間関係なんだー、と夕日に叫びたいお年頃なわけだ。はい、おしまい。おもしろかったか？」
rows.en: “One person like that is more than enough... What I want is an ordinary human relationship! I’m at the age when a boy wants to shout that into the sunset. The end. Did you enjoy it?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And then, on my own, there's so much I... well, better should I say, what I pursue are normal human relatiooons!, that's what I want to scream to the sunset at the time of my life I currently am at. There, all done. Was it interesting?"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese idiom says that even one person like that is already more than enough. The English turns it into a broken statement about the narrator being alone and loses the limit on troublesome relationships.
ghs.remedy: One person like that is already more than enough...

highlights.text: And then, on my own, there's so much I...

rows.jp: 二人はこくこくと頷いた。

ghs.en: Bob bob steady nod in duo.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese simply says that both girls nodded repeatedly. The English is an ungrammatical string of nouns and modifiers rather than an intelligible narrative sentence.
ghs.remedy: The two of them nodded eagerly.

highlights.text: Bob bob steady nod in duo.

rows.jp: 「すっごく、おもしろかった、です」
「……見里先輩も冬子もこの話には目の色変えてたな……女って……」
rows.en: “...Misato and Touko got exactly the same gleam in their eyes when they heard it. Women...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...this story sent both Misato-senpai and Touko in a tizzy... females..."

rows.jp: 「きゃーきゃー」
「きゃーきゃー」
すでに二人はきゃーきゃー話し込んでいる。
rows.en: The two were already deep in excited conversation.

ghs.en: Too late, the two were already deep inside their squee of a conversation.

rows.jp: 黄色い声。
ため息しかつけない。
rows.en: All I could do was sigh.

ghs.en: I could do nothing but sigh.

rows.jp: 結局、全員に話してしまった。
rows.en: In the end, I had told everyone.

ghs.en: And in the end, I told this to everyone in the club, dammit.

rows.jp: 「……なあ美希、とか言ってるうちにそろそろみたいだぞ」
rows.en: “...Miki. While we’ve been talking, I think it’s about time.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...look, Miki, while talking about this and that we're just about to see what you wanted to see now."

rows.jp: 「ぅぇ……あ」
沈んだ日。その光だけが、空をよじのぼって。
rows.en: The sun had sunk, but its light climbed back up the sky.

ghs.en: The sun had sank. Only its light, now, clambers up in the sky.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese presents the sun as already set and its light climbing the sky in one past-tense image. The English uses the ungrammatical past participle 'sank' after 'had' and abruptly shifts the light into present tense.
ghs.remedy: The sun had sunk. Only its light climbed up the sky.

highlights.text: The sun had sank. Only its light, now, clambers up in the sky.

rows.jp: 陽炎のように、空の下半分を染めていた。
rows.en: Like a heat haze, it stained the lower half of heaven.

ghs.en: A shimmer like heat haze dyed the lower half of the sky.

rows.jp: 「へえ」
すごいもんだな。
人はいなくとも世界はまわっているわけだ。
rows.en: The world kept turning, even without people in it.

ghs.en: People are no more, but the world keeps on turning.

rows.jp: 「……うっわぁ」
圧倒的だ。
言葉もなく、三人は光景に魅せられていた。
rows.en: Speechless, the three of us surrendered to the sight.

ghs.en: The three of us are enchanted by a spectacle for which we don't even have words.

rows.jp: やがて。
頓狂な声は、笑っているかのようで―――
rows.en: The odd little sound seemed almost like laughter—

ghs.en: A disarrayed voice, that is just like laughter---

rows.jp: 「あは、ははははははっ」
泣いていた。
俺たちの腕を、強く引き寄せる。
rows.en: She pulled our arms tightly against her.

rows.jp: 「あはははぁ、ひくっ、アハッ……あはぁ……うっ、うっうっう……」
rows.en: “Ahahaha... hic... Ahah... ahaa... ngh, hngh, hngh...”

rows.jp: 「美希、どうしたの？」
「きれいだ……ね……きれ……うわぁぁぁ……」
俺たちは、美希が泣いている理由さえわからず。
rows.en: We did not even know why Miki was crying.

ghs.en: We had no understanding even the reason why Miki was crying,
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says they did not even understand why Miki was crying. The English omits the preposition required by 'understanding' and leaves the sentence grammatically malformed.
ghs.remedy: We didn't even understand why Miki was crying

highlights.text: We had no understanding even the reason why Miki was crying

rows.jp: ただ、困るだけで。
rows.en: All we could do was stand there, helpless.

rows.jp: 「きれいだよっ、きれ……ははっ、ひっく、は…………」

ghs.en: Miki: "It's so beautiful, beaut... hahah, hYk, hah......"

rows.jp: 涙声に見送られて、余光の残像は地平に消えていった。
rows.en: Seen off by her tearful voice, the last image of the afterglow vanished beneath the horizon.

ghs.en: The afterimage of the afterglow vanished towards the horizon, a crying sob biding it farewell.

rows.jp: 「うわあぁぁぁぁぁ―――」
しゃくり上げるばかりだった。

ghs.en: All she did was convulse with sobs.
